parts.text: Which claim about full rounds and leftover distance is correct?

options.text: Full rounds $= 3$ and leftover $= 50$ m along the track, because $800 = 3 \times 250 + 50$.
Call "one round" the leftover distance, and stop before using the $250$ m perimeter.
Report $800$ full rounds, reading the run distance as the round count.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Priya runs on a rectangular track whose perimeter is $250$ m. She runs $800$ m from a start mark that is also the finish line.

part_answers.answer: One full round equals the $250$ m perimeter, so $800 = 3 \times 250 + 50$ means $3$ full rounds and $50$ m left along the track from the finish line.

teacher.key_rationale: Perimeter 250 m; 800 = 3×250 + 50, so 3 full rounds and 50 m leftover. B swaps leftover for one round. C reads the run distance as the round count.
